title: Irreducible components of a locally Noetherian scheme are locally finite
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth]. The family of irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $X$ is locally finite: every point $x\in X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ such that only finitely many irreducible components of $X$ meet $U$.

source.place: Tag 0052, topology-lemma-Noetherian, applied on affine Noetherian open neighbourhoods; its finite-component conclusion gives local finiteness of the irreducible components of X

proof.text: Fix x in X. By the definition of a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], choose an affine open neighbourhood U of x whose ring of sections is Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 0052, topology-lemma-Noetherian, applied on an affine Noetherian open neighbourhood

proof.text: The underlying topological space of U is Noetherian by the affine Noetherian-space theorem [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space]. Therefore it has only finitely many irreducible components [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components].

Every irreducible component C of X that meets U restricts to an irreducible component C intersect U of U, and distinct such components have distinct restrictions, by [lem-sc-components-open-injection]. Hence the irreducible components of X meeting U form a finite set, since they inject into the finite set of irreducible components of U.
The same U is an open neighbourhood of x, so only finitely many irreducible components of X meet U. Since x was arbitrary, the family of irreducible components is locally finite.
